CausalChain: Boronated compounds deliver high LET particles to tumors -> Gadolinium-based agents produce gamma and electron emissions that broaden the irradiation field -> Combined high-LET damage and peripheral low-range radiation induce immunogenic tumor cell death -> Release of tumor-associated antigens and damage-associated molecular patterns -> Activation and recruitment of immune cells -> Enhancement of systemic anti-tumor immunity, especially if paired with checkpoint inhibitors.
Hypothesis: A dual neutron capture therapy combining boronated agents with gadolinium-based nanoparticles will not only improve local cytotoxicity in tumors but also induce immunogenic cell death that primes systemic anti-tumor immune responses, yielding effective abscopal effects when combined with immunotherapy in recurrent or metastatic cancers.
Abstract: We propose a novel dual-agent neutron capture therapeutic strategy that integrates boron-based compounds with gadolinium‐based nanoparticles to not only improve local tumor control but also to stimulate systemic anti‐tumor immune responses. The fusion of two neutron capture modalities, one yielding high linear energy transfer particles confined to tumor cell diameters and the other offering complementary radiation profiles with gamma/x‐ray emissions, could simultaneously achieve precise tumor ablation and immunogenic cell death. When coupled with immunomodulatory agents such as checkpoint inhibitors, this dual strategy has the potential to trigger abscopal effects, offering a promising avenue for treating recurrent and metastatic malignancies.
